scanWindow: Since the 2026-09-14 completed scan, plus material missed developments from the previous 48 hours
notes: Completed the 2026-09-15 editorial scan with no reader-facing publication. Anthropic's September 14 Claude for Financial Advisors launch is independently confirmed by Reuters and supported by launch-partner material describing live wealth-management connectors, but it is a vertical workflow extension closely adjacent to AI Compass's September 11 coverage of ChatGPT for Financial Services; it scores Worth knowing but does not clear today's novelty and broad-reader publication bar. Reuters reporting on a proposed EU Kids Act could become a material governance development if the Commission publishes the proposal, but the draft is still subject to change and no binding measure exists yet, so it remains Watch. Reporting that Palantir, NVIDIA and Booz Allen are tightening use of frontier models over data-retention and proprietary-data concerns is operationally relevant but currently rests on secondary reporting about company practices rather than sufficiently direct primary evidence, so it remains Watch. European political reaction to frontier-slowdown proposals is context on an already logged debate rather than a distinct capability or binding governance change. A former DeepMind researcher's catastrophic-risk warning is commentary rather than a new technical or policy development and is skipped. OpenAI's Data agent in ChatGPT Work was reviewed as an older September 10 launch and not promoted in this run because it predates the active window and overlaps existing enterprise/financial-workspace coverage. Existing Anthropic threat-intelligence, OpenAI financial-services, frontier-safety, Astra and agent-security coverage was deduplicated against the current feed. No rumours, filler, unsupported rankings, unverified pricing or unsourced claims were published.
